subproblem.title: Countable additivity of the co-area identity over disjoint Borel pieces of an injective continuous chart
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Z ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}, and let Z_q (q ∈ ℕ) be pairwise disjoint Borel subsets of ℝ^{n+1} with ⋃_q Z_q = Z. Let ψ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P be continuous on Z and injective on Z, F : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ Borel, and φ, g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] arbitrary. Suppose that for every q the function t ↦ ∫_{ψ(Z_q ∩ F^{−1}(t))} φ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure on ℝ and ∫_ℝ ∫_{ψ(Z_q ∩ F^{−1}(t))} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_{ψ(Z_q)} g dH^{n+1}. Then t ↦ ∫_{ψ(Z ∩ F^{−1}(t))} φ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{ψ(Z ∩ F^{−1}(t))} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_{ψ(Z)} g dH^{n+1}. Here Hᵏ = μHE[k] and all integrals are lower integrals in [0, ∞].

Source. Parent step 3 (reduction to one patch: ψ(Y'∩F^{−1}(t)) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets ψ(Y_q∩F^{−1}(t)); lintegral_iUnion, a.e.-measurability of countable sums and lintegral_tsum), stated for arbitrary disjoint Borel pieces and arbitrary weights.

Conventions: ℝ^k = Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k); e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 is the k-th standard basis vector; for v ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, v(0) = v 0 (Lean `v.ofLp 0`) is its 0-th coordinate, while e_k always denotes a basis vector; DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w; Hᵏ := μHE[k]; |v| := ‖v‖ and |v|ₑ := ‖v‖ₑ = ofReal ‖v‖; all integrals are lower integrals in [0, ∞].

1. (Images.) Each Z_q ⊆ Z (as ⋃_q Z_q = Z). If A ⊆ Z is Borel, ψ(A) is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn: ℝ^{n+1} is Polish and ψ is continuous and injective on A). If A, A' ⊆ Z are disjoint, ψ(A) and ψ(A') are disjoint: ψ(a) = ψ(a') with a ∈ A, a' ∈ A' forces a = a' by injectivity on Z.
2. (Slices.) Fix t ∈ ℝ and put A_q := Z_q ∩ F^{−1}({t}); A_q is Borel (F Borel). The A_q are pairwise disjoint subsets of Z with ⋃_q A_q = Z ∩ F^{−1}({t}), so ψ(Z ∩ F^{−1}(t)) = ⋃_q ψ(A_q) is a countable union of pairwise disjoint Borel sets (step 1). By countable additivity of the lower integral over disjoint measurable sets (lintegral_iUnion, valid for an arbitrary [0, ∞]-valued integrand): ∫_{ψ(Z∩F^{−1}(t))} φ dHⁿ = Σ_q ∫_{ψ(A_q)} φ dHⁿ =: Σ_q f_q(t).
3. (Right side.) Likewise ψ(Z) = ⋃_q ψ(Z_q) is a countable disjoint union of Borel sets, so ∫_{ψ(Z)} g dH^{n+1} = Σ_q ∫_{ψ(Z_q)} g dH^{n+1}.
4. (Measurability.) By step 2, t ↦ ∫_{ψ(Z∩F^{−1}(t))} φ dHⁿ is the function t ↦ Σ_q f_q(t). Each f_q is a.e.-measurable by hypothesis, and a countable sum of a.e.-measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions is a.e.-measurable (AEMeasurable.tsum).
5. (Identity.) ∫_ℝ Σ_q f_q(t) dt = Σ_q ∫_ℝ f_q(t) dt (lintegral_tsum, each f_q a.e.-measurable) = Σ_q ∫_{ψ(Z_q)} g dH^{n+1} (hypothesis) = ∫_{ψ(Z)} g dH^{n+1} (step 3). ∎

subproblem.title: Gram determinant identity det Gram(a₁,…,aₙ) = ‖u‖²·det Gram(a₀,…,aₙ) for the dual vector u (cofactor formula)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let a = (a_0, …, a_n) be vectors of ℝ^P (a : Fin (n+1) → ℝ^P) and u ∈ ℝ^P. Suppose u ∈ span{a_0, …, a_n}, ⟨u, a_0⟩ = 1 and ⟨u, a_{k+1}⟩ = 0 for every k ∈ {0, …, n−1}. Then det[⟨a_{i+1}, a_{j+1}⟩]_{i,j=0}^{n−1} = ‖u‖²·det[⟨a_i, a_j⟩]_{i,j=0}^{n} (the n×n determinant is 1 when n = 0). No linear independence is assumed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (a : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid P) (u : Euclid P), u ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range a) → inner ℝ u (a 0) = 1 → (∀ k : Fin n, inner ℝ u (a k.succ) = 0) → Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n => inner ℝ (a i.succ) (a j.succ)) = ‖u‖ ^ 2 * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (n + 1) => inner ℝ (a i) (a j))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 6 (the Jacobian identity |G(Φ(w))|·JΦ(w) = JΦ_s(z)), in the straightened coordinates of parent step 2 with the distinguished coordinate placed first (i = 0): a_l = DΦ(w)e_l and u = G(Φ(w)). The supplied proof obtains it from the Gram determinant formula (Gram determinant of n+1 vectors = Gram determinant of n of them times the squared distance of the remaining one to their span) and dist(a_0, span{a_1, …, a_n}) = 1/|u|. Departure: the same squared identity det Gram(a_1, …, a_n) = |u|²·det Gram(a_0, …, a_n) is proved here directly by the cofactor (Cramer) formula; this needs no orthogonal projection and no linear independence.

Notation. A := [⟨a_i, a_j⟩]_{i,j=0}^{n} (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (a i) (a j)), A' := [⟨a_{i+1}, a_{j+1}⟩]_{i,j=0}^{n−1} (for n = 0 the empty matrix, determinant 1), δ := (1, 0, …, 0) ∈ ℝ^{n+1} (Pi.single 0 1). The real inner product is symmetric and bilinear.

1. (Coefficients.) Since u ∈ span{a_0, …, a_n}, there is c ∈ ℝ^{n+1} with u = Σ_{l=0}^{n} c_l a_l (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun).
2. (Dual relations.) ⟨u, a_i⟩ = δ_i for every i ∈ {0, …, n}: for i = 0 this is the hypothesis ⟨u, a_0⟩ = 1, and for i = k+1 it is the hypothesis ⟨u, a_{k+1}⟩ = 0 (case split Fin.cases).
3. (A·c = δ.) For every i: (A c)_i = Σ_j ⟨a_i, a_j⟩ c_j = ⟨a_i, Σ_j c_j a_j⟩ = ⟨a_i, u⟩ = ⟨u, a_i⟩ = δ_i, by step 1, symmetry and step 2.
4. (|u|² = c_0.) |u|² = ⟨u, u⟩ = ⟨Σ_l c_l a_l, u⟩ = Σ_l c_l ⟨a_l, u⟩ = Σ_l c_l δ_l = c_0 (steps 1 and 2).
5. (Adjugate.) For every square matrix, adj(A)·A = det(A)·I (Matrix.adjugate_mul). Applying this to c and using step 3: adj(A)·δ = adj(A)·(A·c) = (adj(A)·A)·c = det(A)·c. The 0-th entry of adj(A)·δ is Σ_j adj(A)_{0j} δ_j = adj(A)_{00}; hence adj(A)_{00} = det(A)·c_0.
6. (Cofactor.) By the cofactor description of the adjugate (Matrix.adjugate_fin_succ_eq_det_submatrix), adj(A)_{00} = (−1)^{0+0}·det(A.submatrix (Fin.succAbove 0) (Fin.succAbove 0)). Since Fin.succAbove 0 = Fin.succ, the submatrix has entries A_{i+1, j+1} = ⟨a_{i+1}, a_{j+1}⟩, i.e. it is A'. So adj(A)_{00} = det A'.
7. (Conclusion.) By steps 6, 5 and 4: det A' = det(A)·c_0 = c_0·det A = |u|²·det A, which is the claim Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n => ⟨a i.succ, a j.succ⟩) = ‖u‖² · Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => ⟨a i, a j⟩). ∎

subproblem.title: Slice area formula and Tonelli: ∫_ℝ ∫_{Φ(S∩{w₀=t})} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_S J'·φ∘Φ for an injective immersion Φ of ℝ^{n+1}
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P and S ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} Borel. Assume Φ is differentiable at every w ∈ S with injective derivative DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w, and Φ is injective on S. Let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1, let w(0) be the 0-th coordinate of w, and J'(w) := (det[⟨DΦ(w)e_{i+1}, DΦ(w)e_{j+1}⟩]_{i,j=0}^{n−1})^{1/2} (Real.sqrt). Then for every Borel φ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]: (a) t ↦ ∫_{Φ(S ∩ {w : w(0) = t})} φ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure on ℝ; (b) ∫_ℝ ∫_{Φ(S ∩ {w(0) = t})} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_S ofReal(J'(w))·φ(Φ(w)) dw, the last integral with respect to Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^{n+1}. Here Hⁿ = μHE[n] and all integrals are lower integrals in [0, ∞].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid P) (S : Set (Euclid (n + 1))), MeasurableSet S → (∀ w ∈ S, DifferentiableAt ℝ Φ w) → (∀ w ∈ S, Injective (fderiv ℝ Φ w)) → InjOn Φ S → ∀ φ : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable φ → AEMeasurable (fun t : ℝ => ∫⁻ x in Φ '' (S ∩ {w | w 0 = t}), φ x ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∫⁻ t : ℝ, (∫⁻ x in Φ '' (S ∩ {w | w 0 = t}), φ x ∂μHE[n]) = ∫⁻ w in S, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin n => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single i.succ 1)) (fderiv ℝ Φ w (EuclideanSpace.single j.succ 1))))) * φ (Φ w) ∂volume
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent steps 5 (area formula for every slice parametrization Φ_s) and 7 (Tonelli through the volume-preserving splitting ℝ^{n+1} ≅ ℝ × ℝⁿ), with the distinguished coordinate i = 0, so that ins_0(z, s) = (s, z), drop_0(w) = (w(1), …, w(n)), and the parent's factor JΦ_s(z) is J'(ins_s(z)) below. Departure: the parametrization Φ and the Borel set S are arbitrary (no box B = D × I is needed); the slice of S at a level t is empty when no point of S has first coordinate t.

Conventions: ℝ^k = Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k); e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 is the k-th standard basis vector; for v ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, v(0) = v 0 (Lean `v.ofLp 0`) is its 0-th coordinate, while e_k always denotes a basis vector; DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w; Hᵏ := μHE[k]; |v| := ‖v‖ and |v|ₑ := ‖v‖ₑ = ofReal ‖v‖; all integrals are lower integrals in [0, ∞]. J'(w) := (det[⟨DΦ(w)e_{i+1}, DΦ(w)e_{j+1}⟩]_{i,j=0}^{n−1})^{1/2} (Real.sqrt). For t ∈ ℝ and z ∈ ℝⁿ let ins_t(z) := (t, z_0, …, z_{n−1}) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp z)) ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, and let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+1}, ι(z) := (0, z_0, …, z_{n−1}). ι is linear and continuous (finite dimension), injective (coordinates 1, …, n of ι(z) are those of z), and ι(e'_k) = e_{k+1} for the standard basis vectors e'_k of ℝⁿ. Since ins_t(z) = ins_t(0) + ι(z), ins_t is continuous and injective and has derivative ι at every point (HasFDerivAt.const_add).

1. (J' is Borel.) On the space of continuous linear maps ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P, L ↦ (det[⟨L e_{i+1}, L e_{j+1}⟩])^{1/2} is continuous: the entries are inner products of evaluations, the determinant is a polynomial in the entries, Real.sqrt is continuous. w ↦ DΦ(w) is Borel for every map Φ (measurable_fderiv). Hence J' is Borel.
2. (The integrand H.) Φ is continuous at every point of S (it is differentiable there), so Φ is continuous on S, and the function Φ̃ equal to Φ on S and to 0 off S is Borel (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise, S Borel). Put H := 1_S·ofReal(J')·(φ∘Φ) : ℝ^{n+1} → [0, ∞]. Since H = 1_S·ofReal(J')·(φ∘Φ̃) and φ is Borel, H is Borel.
3. (One slice.) Fix t ∈ ℝ. S_t := ins_t^{−1}(S) ⊆ ℝⁿ is Borel (ins_t is continuous). Put Φ_t := Φ∘ins_t.
 (a) Φ(S ∩ {w : w(0) = t}) = Φ_t(S_t): if w ∈ S and w(0) = t, then w = ins_t(z) for z := (w(1), …, w(n)) (compare coordinates, Fin.cases), so z ∈ S_t and Φ(w) = Φ_t(z); conversely ins_t(z)(0) = t.
 (b) For z ∈ S_t, Φ is differentiable at ins_t(z) ∈ S, so by the chain rule Φ_t is differentiable at z with DΦ_t(z) = DΦ(ins_t(z))∘ι, which is injective as a composition of injective maps.
 (c) Φ_t is injective on S_t: Φ_t(y) = Φ_t(z) with y, z ∈ S_t gives ins_t(y) = ins_t(z) (Φ injective on S), hence ι(y) = ι(z) and y = z.
 (d) By the sibling gram_area_formula with m := n, f := Φ_t, s := S_t and weight φ: ∫_{Φ_t(S_t)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{S_t} ofReal(J_t(z))·φ(Φ_t(z)) dz with J_t(z) = (det[⟨DΦ_t(z)e'_k, DΦ_t(z)e'_l⟩])^{1/2}. By (b) and ι(e'_k) = e_{k+1}, DΦ_t(z)e'_k = DΦ(ins_t(z))e_{k+1}, so J_t(z) = J'(ins_t(z)).
 (e) Since 1_{S_t}(z) = 1_S(ins_t(z)) (lintegral_indicator, S_t Borel), (a) and (d) give, for every t ∈ ℝ: ∫_{Φ(S ∩ {w(0) = t})} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} H(ins_t(z)) dz.
4. (Volume-preserving splitting.) E : ℝ × ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+1}, E(t, z) := ins_t(z), is the composition of (id × WithLp.ofLp) : ℝ × ℝⁿ → ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ) (measure preserving by PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp and MeasurePreserving.prod), of the inverse of MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) 0, which maps (t, g) to Fin.cons t g (measure preserving by volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove), and of WithLp.toLp 2 (measure preserving by PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp). So E is measure preserving from the product Lebesgue measure on ℝ × ℝⁿ to Lebesgue measure on ℝ^{n+1}; in particular H∘E is Borel.
5. (Claim (a).) By Tonelli's measurability statement (Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'; Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ is s-finite), t ↦ ∫_{ℝⁿ} H(E(t, z)) dz is Borel. By step 3(e) it equals t ↦ ∫_{Φ(S ∩ {w(0) = t})} φ dHⁿ, which is therefore Borel, hence a.e.-measurable.
6. (Claim (b).) ∫_ℝ ∫_{Φ(S ∩ {w(0) = t})} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_ℝ ∫_{ℝⁿ} H(E(t, z)) dz dt (step 3(e)) = ∫_{ℝ×ℝⁿ} H∘E (Tonelli, lintegral_prod) = ∫_{ℝ^{n+1}} H dw (E measure preserving and H Borel, MeasurePreserving.lintegral_comp) = ∫_S ofReal(J'(w))·φ(Φ(w)) dw (lintegral_indicator, S Borel). ∎

subproblem.title: Countable cover of {DF ≠ 0} by C¹ straightening charts Ψ_q with F∘Ψ_q = first coordinate
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and F : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ be C¹. Then there are sets B_q ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} and maps Ψ_q : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} (q ∈ ℕ) such that for every q: B_q is open; Ψ_q is C¹ on B_q and injective on B_q; the derivative DΨ_q(w) = fderiv ℝ Ψ_q w is bijective for every w ∈ B_q; F(Ψ_q(w)) = w(0) (the 0-th coordinate of w) for every w ∈ B_q; Ψ_q(B_q) is open; and {y ∈ ℝ^{n+1} : DF(y) ≠ 0} ⊆ ⋃_q Ψ_q(B_q).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Euclid (n + 1) → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 F → ∃ (B : ℕ → Set (Euclid (n + 1))) (Ψ : ℕ → Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)), (∀ q, IsOpen (B q)) ∧ (∀ q, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (Ψ q) (B q)) ∧ (∀ q, InjOn (Ψ q) (B q)) ∧ (∀ q, ∀ w ∈ B q, Bijective (fderiv ℝ (Ψ q) w)) ∧ (∀ q, ∀ w ∈ B q, F (Ψ q w) = w 0) ∧ (∀ q, IsOpen (Ψ q '' B q)) ∧ {y | fderiv ℝ F y ≠ 0} ⊆ ⋃ q, Ψ q '' B q

Conventions: ℝ^k = Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k); e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 is the k-th standard basis vector; for v ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, v(0) = v 0 (Lean `v.ofLp 0`) is its 0-th coordinate, while e_k always denotes a basis vector; DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w; Hᵏ := μHE[k]; |v| := ‖v‖ and |v|ₑ := ‖v‖ₑ = ofReal ‖v‖; all integrals are lower integrals in [0, ∞].

1. (A good coordinate.) Let y₀ ∈ ℝ^{n+1} with DF(y₀) ≠ 0. There is i ∈ {0, …, n} with DF(y₀)e_i ≠ 0: otherwise DF(y₀)v = Σ_j v_j·DF(y₀)e_j = 0 for every v (v = Σ_j v_j e_j), i.e. DF(y₀) = 0.
2. (The straightening map.) Let L : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1}, L(y) := (0, y(i.succAbove 0), …, y(i.succAbove (n−1))) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 0 (k ↦ y(i.succAbove k))); L is linear (check coordinatewise, Fin.cases), hence a continuous linear map. Let Θ(y) := F(y)·e_0 + L(y). Then Θ(y)(0) = F(y) and Θ(y)(k+1) = y(i.succAbove k). Θ is C¹ (F is C¹ and L is linear) with DΘ(y)h = (DF(y)h)·e_0 + L(h) (HasFDerivAt.smul_const, HasFDerivAt.add).
3. (DΘ(y₀) is injective.) Let DΘ(y₀)h = 0. Coordinate k+1 gives h(i.succAbove k) = 0 for every k < n. Every index j is i or i.succAbove k for some k (Fin.eq_self_or_eq_succAbove), so h = h(i)·e_i. Coordinate 0 gives 0 = DF(y₀)h = h(i)·DF(y₀)e_i, so h(i) = 0 by step 1, i.e. h = 0. As DΘ(y₀) is linear, it is injective.
4. (Local inverse.) Apply the sibling local_inverse with d := n + 1, φ := Θ, V := ℝ^{n+1} (open, contains y₀, Θ is C¹ on it) and z₀ := y₀. It gives open sets V₀ ∋ y₀ and O and a map χ, C¹ on O, with χ(O) ⊆ V₀, Θ(χ(a)) = a for a ∈ O, and Θ(z) ∈ O and χ(Θ(z)) = z for z ∈ V₀.
5. (Properties of (O, χ).) (a) χ is injective on O: χ(a) = χ(b) gives a = Θ(χ(a)) = Θ(χ(b)) = b. (b) χ(O) = V₀: ⊆ holds by step 4; if z ∈ V₀ then z = χ(Θ(z)) with Θ(z) ∈ O. So χ(O) is open and contains y₀. (c) For a ∈ O: F(χ(a)) = Θ(χ(a))(0) = a(0). (d) For a ∈ O: χ is differentiable at a (C¹ on the open set O), Θ is differentiable at χ(a), and Θ∘χ = id on the neighbourhood O of a, so D(Θ∘χ)(a) = D(id)(a) = id (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). By the chain rule DΘ(χ(a))∘Dχ(a) = id, so Dχ(a) is injective, and an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^{n+1} is surjective (LinearMap.surjective_of_injective); so Dχ(a) is bijective.
 Thus every y₀ in O' := {y : DF(y) ≠ 0} has data (B_{y₀}, Ψ_{y₀}) := (O, χ) with B_{y₀} open, Ψ_{y₀} C¹ and injective on B_{y₀}, DΨ_{y₀}(w) bijective and F(Ψ_{y₀}(w)) = w(0) for w ∈ B_{y₀}, and N_{y₀} := Ψ_{y₀}(B_{y₀}) open with y₀ ∈ N_{y₀}.
6. (Countable subfamily.) Choose such data for every y ∈ O'. The sets N_y (y ∈ O') are open and ℝ^{n+1} is second countable, so there is a countable T ⊆ O' with ⋃_{y∈T} N_y = ⋃_{y∈O'} N_y (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). Since y ∈ N_y for y ∈ O', O' ⊆ ⋃_{y∈T} N_y.
7. (Enumeration.) If T ≠ ∅, write T = {y_q : q ∈ ℕ} (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range) and put (B_q, Ψ_q) := (B_{y_q}, Ψ_{y_q}); every required property holds by step 5, and O' ⊆ ⋃_{y∈T} N_y = ⋃_q Ψ_q(B_q) by step 6. If T = ∅, then O' ⊆ ⋃_{y∈T} N_y = ∅; put B_q := ∅ and Ψ_q := id: ∅ is open, id is C¹ and injective on ∅, the pointwise conditions are vacuous, id(∅) = ∅ is open, and O' = ∅ ⊆ ⋃_q Ψ_q(B_q). ∎

Conventions: ℝ^k = Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k); e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 is the k-th standard basis vector; for v ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, v(0) = v 0 (Lean `v.ofLp 0`) is its 0-th coordinate, while e_k always denotes a basis vector; DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w; Hᵏ := μHE[k]; |v| := ‖v‖ and |v|ₑ := ‖v‖ₑ = ofReal ‖v‖; all integrals are lower integrals in [0, ∞]. J(w) := (det[⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩]_{i,j=0}^{n})^{1/2} and J'(w) := (det[⟨DΦ(w)e_{i+1}, DΦ(w)e_{j+1}⟩]_{i,j=0}^{n−1})^{1/2} (Real.sqrt).

1. (Slices.) By slice_tonelli applied to Φ, S and φ (its hypotheses are among ours): t ↦ ∫_{Φ(S ∩ {w : w(0) = t})} φ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable, which is the first claim, and ∫_ℝ ∫_{Φ(S ∩ {w(0) = t})} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_S ofReal(J'(w))·φ(Φ(w)) dw.
2. (Area formula.) By gram_area_formula with m := n + 1, f := Φ, s := S and weight g := |G|ₑ·φ (no measurability of g is needed): ∫_{Φ(S)} |G|ₑ·φ dH^{n+1} = ∫_S ofReal(J(w))·(|G(Φ(w))|ₑ·φ(Φ(w))) dw.
3. (Jacobian identity at w ∈ S.) Put a_l := DΦ(w)e_l (l = 0, …, n) and u := G(Φ(w)).
 (a) u ∈ span{a_0, …, a_n}: by hypothesis u = DΦ(w)v for some v ∈ ℝ^{n+1}; v = Σ_l v_l e_l, so u = Σ_l v_l a_l by linearity (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun).
 (b) By the hypothesis ⟨u, DΦ(w)e⟩ = e(0): ⟨u, a_0⟩ = e_0(0) = 1 and ⟨u, a_{k+1}⟩ = e_{k+1}(0) = 0 for k < n.
 (c) By gram_cofactor: det[⟨a_{i+1}, a_{j+1}⟩] = |u|²·det[⟨a_i, a_j⟩]. Taking real square roots, with √(x·y) = √x·√y for x = |u|² ≥ 0 (Real.sqrt_mul) and √(|u|²) = |u|: J'(w) = |u|·J(w).
 (d) Hence ofReal(J'(w))·φ(Φ(w)) = ofReal(|u|)·ofReal(J(w))·φ(Φ(w)) = ofReal(J(w))·(|G(Φ(w))|ₑ·φ(Φ(w))) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, |u| ≥ 0; ofReal |u| = |u|ₑ; commutativity in [0, ∞]).
4. (Conclusion.) By 3(d) the integrands in steps 1 and 2 agree at every point of the Borel set S, so the two integrals over S agree (setLIntegral_congr_fun). With step 1 this gives ∫_ℝ ∫_{Φ(S ∩ {w(0) = t})} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_{Φ(S)} |G|ₑ·φ dH^{n+1}. ∎

subproblem.title: Co-area formula on one straightened patch Z ⊆ Ψ(B) of a C¹ chart ψ
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} be open, ψ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P C¹ on V and injective on V with Dψ(y) injective for every y ∈ V, and F : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ C¹. Let B ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} be open and Ψ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} C¹ on B and injective on B, with DΨ(w) bijective and F(Ψ(w)) = w(0) for every w ∈ B. Let Z ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} be Borel with Z ⊆ V and Z ⊆ Ψ(B), and let G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P satisfy, for every y ∈ Z, G(ψ(y)) ∈ Dψ(y)(ℝ^{n+1}) and ⟨G(ψ(y)), Dψ(y)e⟩ = DF(y)e for every e ∈ ℝ^{n+1}. Then for every Borel φ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]: t ↦ ∫_{ψ(Z ∩ F^{−1}(t))} φ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure on ℝ, and ∫_ℝ ∫_{ψ(Z ∩ F^{−1}(t))} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_{ψ(Z)} |G|·φ dH^{n+1}. Here Hᵏ = μHE[k], |G| = ‖G‖ₑ and all integrals are lower integrals in [0, ∞].

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step 4 (one patch: Φ := ψ∘Ψ, Ŷ := Θ(Y_q) = B ∩ Ψ^{−1}(Y_q), ψ(Y_q) = Φ(Ŷ) and ψ(Y_q ∩ F^{−1}(s)) = Φ(Ŷ ∩ {w(0) = s})) together with the hypothesis check of step 6 (⟨u, DΦ(w)e_l⟩ = DF(y)DΨ(w)e_l = ∂_l(F∘Ψ)(w)); the patch identity itself is the sibling param_coarea. Departure: as in straightening_cover the straightened coordinate is the first one (F(Ψ(w)) = w(0)), and the patch is described as S := B ∩ Ψ^{−1}(Z) for an arbitrary Borel Z ⊆ V ∩ Ψ(B).

Conventions: ℝ^k = Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k); e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 is the k-th standard basis vector; for v ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, v(0) = v 0 (Lean `v.ofLp 0`) is its 0-th coordinate, while e_k always denotes a basis vector; DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w; Hᵏ := μHE[k]; |v| := ‖v‖ and |v|ₑ := ‖v‖ₑ = ofReal ‖v‖; all integrals are lower integrals in [0, ∞].

1. (Differentiability.) Ψ is differentiable at every w ∈ B and ψ at every y ∈ V (C¹ on open sets: ContDiffOn.differentiableOn and IsOpen.mem_nhds).
2. (S is Borel.) Let S := B ∩ Ψ^{−1}(Z) and let Ψ̃ equal Ψ on B and 0 off B. Ψ is continuous on the open (Borel) set B, so Ψ̃ is Borel (ContinuousOn.measurable_piecewise), and S = B ∩ Ψ̃^{−1}(Z) is Borel.
3. (Φ := ψ∘Ψ on S.) Let w ∈ S; then Ψ(w) ∈ Z ⊆ V. By the chain rule Φ is differentiable at w with DΦ(w) = Dψ(Ψ(w))∘DΨ(w); it is injective since Dψ(Ψ(w)) is injective (Ψ(w) ∈ V) and DΨ(w) is bijective. Φ is injective on S: Φ(a) = Φ(b) gives Ψ(a) = Ψ(b) (ψ injective on V) and then a = b (Ψ injective on B).
4. (D(F∘Ψ) is the first coordinate on B.) Let w ∈ B. On the open neighbourhood B of w, F∘Ψ coincides with the continuous linear map π_0 : v ↦ v(0) (EuclideanSpace.proj 0), so D(F∘Ψ)(w) = π_0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq; a continuous linear map is its own derivative). F is differentiable everywhere and Ψ at w, so by the chain rule DF(Ψ(w))(DΨ(w)e) = e(0) for every e ∈ ℝ^{n+1}.
5. (Hypotheses of param_coarea.) Let w ∈ S and y := Ψ(w) ∈ Z. (a) By hypothesis G(ψ(y)) = Dψ(y)v for some v; DΨ(w) is surjective, so v = DΨ(w)u for some u, and G(Φ(w)) = Dψ(y)(DΨ(w)u) = DΦ(w)u ∈ DΦ(w)(ℝ^{n+1}). (b) For every e: ⟨G(Φ(w)), DΦ(w)e⟩ = ⟨G(ψ(y)), Dψ(y)(DΨ(w)e)⟩ = DF(y)(DΨ(w)e) = e(0), by the hypothesis on G and step 4.
6. (Apply param_coarea.) By param_coarea with Φ, S, G and φ (hypotheses: steps 2, 3, 5): t ↦ ∫_{Φ(S ∩ {w : w(0) = t})} φ dHⁿ is a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{Φ(S ∩ {w(0) = t})} φ dHⁿ dt = ∫_{Φ(S)} |G|ₑ·φ dH^{n+1}.
7. (Back to the chart.) Ψ(S) = Z: Ψ(S) ⊆ Z by definition; if y ∈ Z ⊆ Ψ(B) then y = Ψ(w) with w ∈ B, and w ∈ S. Hence Φ(S) = ψ(Ψ(S)) = ψ(Z). For t ∈ ℝ, Ψ(S ∩ {w(0) = t}) = Z ∩ F^{−1}(t), because F(Ψ(w)) = w(0) for w ∈ B (same two inclusions). Hence Φ(S ∩ {w(0) = t}) = ψ(Z ∩ F^{−1}(t)).
8. Substituting step 7 into step 6 gives both claims. ∎
